flags.title: McGirt Decision (2020) — Half of Eastern Oklahoma Is Indian Country
flags.summary: The US Supreme Court's McGirt v. Oklahoma (2020) decision confirmed that much of eastern Oklahoma — including Tulsa — remains Indian Country under the jurisdiction of the Muscogee (Creek) Nation and other tribes. This affects criminal jurisdiction, tribal court authority, and program eligibility. Muscogee Nation: 918-732-7600 / mcn-nsn.gov. Cherokee Nation: 918-453-5000 / cherokee.org.

flags.title: 39 Federally Recognized Tribes — Most Complex Tribal Landscape in Continental US
flags.summary: Oklahoma has 39 federally recognized tribes — the most complex tribal landscape in the continental United States. Each tribe has its own governance, courts, and social services. Always verify tribal enrollment and jurisdiction before routing. Oklahoma Indian Legal Services: 405-943-6457 / oilsinc.org.

flags.title: Tulsa Greenwood District — Historic Black Wall Street, Ongoing Reparations Case
flags.summary: The Greenwood District in Tulsa was the site of the 1921 Tulsa Race Massacre. Reparations litigation is ongoing. The area has concentrated poverty and historical disinvestment. Tulsa Community Action Project: 918-382-3200 / tulsacap.org. Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma: 918-584-3211 / legalaidok.org.

flags.title: SoonerCare Plus Expansion (2021) — Stable But Monitor
flags.summary: Oklahoma expanded Medicaid (SoonerCare) in 2021 via ballot initiative. Enrollment is stable but political opposition continues. Adults 19-64 up to 138% FPL eligible. SoonerCare: 800-987-7767 / okhca.org.

flags.title: 3-Year Wage SOL — OK Protection of Labor Act
flags.summary: Oklahoma Protection of Labor Act provides a 3-year statute of limitations for wage claims — longer than federal FLSA (2 years). Dual-file state and federal. OK DOL: 405-521-6100 / ok.gov/odol.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Oklahoma Emergency Detention
flags.message: OK involuntary psychiatric hold law: Oklahoma Emergency Detention. Statutory authority: 43A O.S. § 5-207. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in OK retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in OK: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Oklahoma Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Oklahoma Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
